key_insight: CoReMem treats memory as an investment: information carried between coding tasks should justify the effort required to write and read it. It connects memory selection with an agent’s decision about when using that memory can save work.
problem_solved: Coding agents work through successive tasks in changing repositories, but must prepare memory before knowing the next task. They need to balance uncertain future usefulness against memory overhead and decide when available memory is worth using.
method: Introduce Coding-Repository Memory (CoReMem), a framework for managing memory across successive coding tasks.
Account for memory-writing and memory-reading costs when judging the prospective value of retained information.
Guide memory design and actor adaptation so agents can decide when acting on memory is likely to reduce effort.
impact: For AI coding practitioners, CoReMem offers a way to reason about useful memory rather than simply accumulating more context. The provided abstract is truncated, so quantitative savings and performance gains cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Task timeline showing repository edits and memory carried from one coding task to the next.
Balance scale contrasting expected future usefulness with memory-writing and memory-reading costs.
Decision flowchart showing an agent choosing whether to use available memory as a task unfolds.
Memory investment loop: retain information → evaluate usefulness on later tasks → inform future memory choices.
paper_title: CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation
paper_authors: Peiwen Li, Harshit Verma, Sophia Zhou, Haiwen Wang, Ngoc Bui
